“Southern Hemisphere humpback whale feeding aggregations have been identified for the first time, in the Benguela upwelling system, off southern Namibia and South Africa, during the Southern Hemisphere spring.”

“Large, tightly spaced groups (20 to >200 individuals) of Southern Hemisphere humpsback whales (Megapetra novaeanglia) were observed feeding on Euphausiids and mantis shrimp in the southern Benguela Upweling system during October/November 2001, 2014 and 2015.

“We have identified a novel, inter-annual feeding aggregation pattern for humpback whales in the southern Benguela Upweling System, which has the potential to provide new insight into Southern Hemisphere feeding behaviours.”

humpback whales are capable of feeding in the low-latitude waters of the southern Benguala System, where they are not known to have been feeding in the past.
